newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Meridor says Israel budget deficit under forecast.
newsitem.headline: Meridor says Israel budget deficit under forecast.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Sunday that the government's budget deficit was under forecast in October, the second month in a row.

He said Treasury officials had expected a shortfall of 1.5 billion shekels, but earlier on Sunday the Treasury reported that the deficit was 1.03 billion shekels, bringing the total for the first 10 months of the year to 9.78 billion shekels, excluding credits granted by the government.
The budget originally called for a deficit of 7.6 billion shekels for the full year.
The Treasury has been monitoring the deficit situation especially closely because the extent of this year's overspending will determine whether it has to seek additional bugdet cuts in 1997.
The 1997 budget is now in parliament where it has met very strong opposition on grounds that the 4.9 billion in cuts included in it will hurt lower-income groups.
Meridor said he would decide on the need for further spending reductions based on the deficit situation in the last part of the current year.

Meridor said that on Friday he had agreed on the guidelines for discussions over the next few weeks about making adjustments to the 1997 spending package to help the poor and disadvantaged. He vowed not to let next year's deficit exceed the target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
